subject.title: [Feature]: Automatic Output Sanitization for Sensitive Data

question: Should OpenClaw add a core automatic final-output sanitization boundary, and where should it run relative to tool results, response generation, plugin hooks, and channel delivery?
rationale: The security goal is valid, but the default scope, false-positive tolerance, config surface, and interaction with existing redaction and SecretRef boundaries require maintainer intent before implementation.

options.title: Design a core boundary
options.body: Define a security-reviewed core sanitizer that reuses existing redaction infrastructure and starts with a documented, tested scope across final replies and adjacent sinks.

options.title: Expose plugin hooks first
options.body: Keep core policy minimal and add only the missing extension points for an official or community sanitizer plugin to own detection patterns and output behavior.

options.title: Limit to existing redaction surfaces
options.body: Decline final-output filtering for now and document that users should rely on SecretRefs, log/tool redaction, and explicit skills/plugins instead.

recommendation.title: Design a core boundary
recommendation.body: Define a security-reviewed core sanitizer that reuses existing redaction infrastructure and starts with a documented, tested scope across final replies and adjacent sinks.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the CODEOWNERS-routed security boundary most directly responsible for secrets and credential exposure decisions.
